rationale: Whole dried Zahedi dates were fed in one of four groups of six. Hot-plate latency was shorter from month one to month two in the date arm, with no clear date-versus-chow or within-arm difference. Evoked thermal latency remains a remote Parkinson pain outcome.

After each period the abdominal-pain values were 0.22 versus 0.25. No clear difference or paired interval was reported. Masking differed between the publication and registry, with healthy participants and a low-symptom abdominal diary.

Evoked writhing and hot-plate tests favored the three ethanol extracts. They also reduced movement and prolonged drug-induced sleep. Assays have five per group and do not measure whole fruit or Parkinson pain.

The warm-surface response favored fresh date extract and the tail-flick endpoint was inconclusive. The report disagrees about significance and route details. The disease model and preparation differ from the claim.
Original author results include symptom timing without a transferable between-group cramp-severity estimate. Related articles may draw on the same people.
A multicomponent bar assigns shared date paste and the planned total includes a pain item. The separate listed item targets constipation, with no pain result posted.
The single-arm pilot reports aggregate and gastrointestinal findings. The original bar's date content and pain-item effect remain unverified.
The modern survey counts immune-support reports. Historical headache use is cited independently of its participants and no outcome is observed.

A registered migraine study plans oral date-palm distillate against placebo. Its outcome wording conflicts across product label, scale and timepoint fields, and it reports no results for either group.

Date syrup was compared with water during labor. VAS means at 60 minutes were 7.77 and 9.05 (p=.001). Taste and energy were uncontrolled. Companion reports share the registry with participant totals that differ. Acute labor and the processed drink limit transfer.

Within saffron, replacing artificial sweetener with date juice gave an inconclusive during-labor contrast of −0.3 on the 0–10 VAS (95% CI −1.0 to 0.4). There was a one-hour postpartum difference. The two comparisons use different periods and analyses. Saffron, preparation and population limit transfer.

Stage-two pain scores were 7.25 with date syrup, 7.67 with honey-saffron syrup and 8.47 with placebo. Masking is inconsistently described and the registry omits a separate pain outcome. The progress report is the same cohort. Acute obstetric pain and syrup differ from the claim.

Improvement in abdominal pain was reported for 15/47, 15/42 and 13/42 in the three-, five- and no-date groups (p=.883). The registered allocation conflicts with the author account. Whole fruit improves preparation fit while the child cohort and specific abdominal outcome limit transfer.
